1.title: Governance, Risk and Compliance, Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery
1.text: Welcome to Module five: Governance, Risk and Compliance, Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery. It covers the exam area two. Security Governance. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. two point one Plan Governance, Risk, and Compliance (G R C): Purpose. Importance. Frameworks and tools. two point two Understand redundancy: Business Continuity (B C). Disaster Recovery (D R). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two. Security Governance (seventeen point three percent). Exam format: an adaptive exam of one hundred to one hundred twenty-five questions in two hours; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official I S C two C C exam outline.

1.title: Governance, risk and compliance (GRC)
1.text: Governance, risk and compliance (G R C). G R C brings three things together so the organization reaches its goals reliably, manages uncertainty and acts with integrity. Governance. Question: Who decides, and what is the direction? Example: Board-approved security strategy and policies. Risk. Question: What could go wrong, and how bad? Example: Risk register and treatment plans. Compliance. Question: Are we following the rules? Example: Audits against laws, standards and policies.

1.title: Governance, risk and compliance (GRC), continued
1.text: Governance, risk and compliance (G R C). Purpose. Align security with business goals, manage risk, prove compliance. Importance. Avoid fines and loss, make informed decisions, build trust. Frameworks and tools. nist C S F (critical success factor), I S O I E C twenty-seven thousand one, C O B I T; G R C platforms that hold the risk register, policies, evidence and audit tasks. Exam tip: G R C is one program, not three. Its goal is decisions based on risk that also meet the rules.

1.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
1.text: Business continuity and disaster recovery. The figure shows this: Business continuity keeps the business running; disaster recovery restores I T.

1.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery, continued
1.text: Business continuity and disaster recovery. Business continuity plan (B C P). Scope: The whole business: people, process, sites. Goal: Keep critical functions running during a disruption. Disaster recovery plan (D R P). Scope: I T systems and data. Goal: Restore them after a disaster. Incident response plan (I R P). Scope: A security incident. Goal: Detect, contain and recover (Module fifteen). A business impact analysis (B I A) comes first: it finds the critical functions, their dependencies and the cost of downtime.

1.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery, continued
1.text: Business continuity and disaster recovery. Maximum tolerable downtime (M T D) (or M A O). The longest outage the business can survive. Recovery time objective (R T O). The target time to restore a system; shorter than the M T D. Recovery point objective (R P O). The most data you can lose, measured in time since the last backup. Exam tip: R T O equals how long to be back. R P O equals how much data to lose. B I A first, then the plans.

1.title: Redundancy and recovery options
1.text: Redundancy and recovery options. Redundancy. Spare capacity so one failure does not stop service: raid, clustering, failover, load balancing, dual power, U P S and generators. Hot site. Fully equipped and running; recovery in minutes to hours; most expensive. Warm site. Equipment ready, data must be loaded; hours to days. Cold site. Space and power only; days to weeks; cheapest. Cloud recovery. Rebuild in the cloud on demand.

1.title: Redundancy and recovery options, continued
1.text: Redundancy and recovery options. Full. What it copies: Everything. Restore needs: The latest full backup. Differential. What it copies: Changes since the last full. Restore needs: Last full plus the latest differential. Incremental. What it copies: Changes since the last backup of any kind. Restore needs: Last full plus every incremental since. three, two, one rule: three copies, on two kinds of media, one off site. A backup you have not tested is a hope, not a plan.

1.title: Testing the plans and the AI angle
1.text: Testing the plans and the A I angle. Read-through or checklist. What happens: Team reads the plan. Disruption: None. Tabletop (walkthrough). What happens: Team talks through a scenario. Disruption: None. Simulation. What happens: Acts out a scenario. Disruption: Low. Parallel. What happens: Systems are recovered at the alternate site while production runs. Disruption: Low. Full interruption. What happens: Production is shut down and the alternate site takes over. Disruption: High. A I and recovery: back up A I configurations and datasets, not only traditional data. Model drift, a decline in A I performance over time, is a business continuity risk because operations that rely on the model suffer. Exam tip: Tabletop exercises are discussion only; full interruption is the riskiest test. Hot equals fast and costly; cold equals slow and cheap.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A company must be able to lose no more than one hour of data after a failure. Which metric states this requirement? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Recovery point objective of one hour. The recovery point objective is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which plan focuses on keeping the critical functions of the whole business running during a disruption? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The business continuity plan, which covers the business. The business continuity plan covers the whole business; the disaster recovery plan restores I T.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A bank needs a recovery site that can take over within minutes and accepts the highest cost. Which site fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A hot site that is fully equipped and running. A hot site is ready to take over within minutes to hours and is the most expensive option.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which analysis should be done first to find the critical business functions and the cost of downtime? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Business impact analysis. The business impact analysis identifies critical functions and drives the recovery objectives.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team reads a scenario aloud around a table and decides who would do what, without touching any system. What type of test is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Tabletop exercise that only discusses the scenario. A tabletop or walkthrough exercise is a discussion and does not disrupt operations.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A company uses an A I model to approve orders, and over several months the model's accuracy falls. Which risk does this describe? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Model drift, a continuity risk for the operation. Model drift is a decline in A I performance that can harm operations, so it belongs in continuity planning.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does R T O measure? Answer: The target time to restore a system. Question two. Which site is the cheapest and slowest? Answer: A cold site. Question three. What does the three, two, one rule say? Answer: Three copies, two media, one off site.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What must be restored after a differential backup? Answer: The last full backup plus the latest differential. Question five. What comes before the B C P and D R P? Answer: The business impact analysis. Question six. Which test shuts production down? Answer: The full interruption test.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. G R C: governance (direction), risk, compliance; one program. Plans: B C P (business), D R P (I T), I R P (security incident). Metrics: M T D (longest outage), R T O (time back), R P O (data loss). Sites: hot (fast, costly), warm, cold (slow, cheap). Backups: full, differential, incremental; three, two, one; test restores. Tests: read-through, tabletop, simulation, parallel, full interruption. A I: back up configs and datasets; model drift is a risk.
